name: Understanding biodiversity net gain
fact: Defra guidance updated 14 July 2026 explains mandatory BNG, the 10% objective, 30-year habitat management, the biodiversity gain hierarchy, the 6 August 2026 small-development changes and the 2 November 2026 NSIP start date.
gate: BNG applicability and delivery route must be resolved for the exact application date and development type; a generic 10% rule is not parcel-level approval or deliverability evidence.

name: Biodiversity net gain guidance collection
fact: The Defra collection links current developer, land manager, LPA, metric, statutory credit, gain-site register and NSIP BNG guidance.
gate: A guidance index is authoritative context but does not establish that a target development has complied with BNG requirements.

name: Biodiversity net gain exempt developments
fact: From 6 August 2026 BNG does not apply to planning applications for development sites of 0.2 hectares or below; the guidance also defines de minimis, temporary and other exemptions with priority-habitat caveats.
gate: Apply exemptions only using the exact application date, red-line area, habitat impact and exemption conditions; do not infer exemption from approximate site size.

name: Calculate biodiversity value with the statutory biodiversity metric
fact: Guidance updated 14 July 2026 identifies the statutory biodiversity metric as the official BNG calculation method and says competent ecological input is generally required outside qualifying small-site metric cases.
gate: Metric output depends on surveyed habitat inputs and does not itself approve a biodiversity gain plan, legal agreement or development.

name: Statutory biodiversity metric tools and guides
fact: Defra's official metric tools page was updated 2 June 2026 and states that updates are recorded in version history and that the statutory tools also apply to NSIPs from 2 November 2026.
gate: Tool availability or version choice is not evidence that the site habitat baseline or condition assessment is correct.

name: Biodiversity net gain planning practice guidance
fact: Planning practice guidance states BNG is generally a post-permission matter: unless exempt, the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be approved before development commences, and registered off-site gains or purchased credits in the plan must be evidenced.
gate: Planning permission is not discharge of the biodiversity gain condition; gain-plan approval is a separate legal state.

name: Biodiversity net gain: what local planning authorities should do
fact: Updated 14 July 2026, the guidance sets what LPAs must check at application stage, when reviewing and approving Biodiversity Gain Plans, and during BNG monitoring.
gate: Submission of a metric or gain plan is not approval; LPA review and the statutory biodiversity gain condition remain separate.

name: Meet biodiversity net gain requirements: steps for developers
fact: The official developer workflow separates planning permission, on-site/off-site delivery, statutory-credit use, habitat management and submission of the Biodiversity Gain Plan.
gate: Completion of an early workflow step does not imply later BNG legal, registration, allocation or approval steps are complete.

name: Make on-site biodiversity gains as a developer
fact: Updated 14 July 2026, the guidance explains on-site BNG, significant enhancements and the hierarchy, including the 6 August 2026 change allowing qualifying small developments to consider on-site and off-site options together.
gate: Potential on-site habitat enhancement is not secured BNG until metric, legal/condition requirements and approved gain-plan evidence exist.

name: Make off-site biodiversity gains as a developer
fact: Official guidance requires off-site gains to be registered and allocated to the development, with the gain-site reference included in the Biodiversity Gain Plan; off-site gains must be maintained for at least 30 years.
gate: Buying or identifying off-site units is not enough; registration, allocation, legal security and gain-plan approval must be verified.

name: Submit a biodiversity gain plan
fact: The gain-plan guidance requires the metric, pre- and post-development plans and, where relevant, irreplaceable-habitat compensation, off-site register references, statutory-credit proof and habitat management information.
gate: A submitted Biodiversity Gain Plan is not an approved plan or permission to commence development.

name: Register a biodiversity gain site
fact: Updated 2 June 2026, the Natural England registration process requires legal-security and habitat-management evidence and says accepted sites receive a unique gain-site reference.
gate: An application to register a gain site is not acceptance; registration is also separate from allocating units to a particular development.

name: Search the biodiversity gain sites register
fact: The national register exposes accepted gain-site location, boundary, habitats, allocations and responsible authority/body information supplied through accepted applications.
gate: Register presence does not prove that unallocated units remain available, that a target development has secured them, or that its gain plan is approved.

name: Record allocation of off-site biodiversity gains to a development
fact: Updated 2 June 2026, the service records specific off-site biodiversity gains against a development after gain-site registration.
gate: Gain-site registration and allocation are distinct; neither alone proves the Biodiversity Gain Plan has been approved or development can commence.

name: Register a biodiversity site and allocate to a development
fact: Natural England provides a combined route to register a gain site and record off-site allocation to a development with planning permission at the same time.
gate: Use of the combined service is an application process, not proof that registration/allocation was accepted or the planning BNG condition discharged.

name: Enter a legal agreement for biodiversity net gain
fact: Updated 2 June 2026, guidance explains planning obligations and conservation covenants used to secure on-site or off-site gains for at least 30 years and notes enforcement can follow non-compliance.
gate: A draft HMMP or habitat proposal does not replace the required legal security where legal security is required.

name: Creating a habitat management and monitoring plan for BNG
fact: Updated 2 June 2026, the guidance says HMMPs support long-term management and monitoring but do not replace the legal agreement securing BNG habitat obligations.
gate: HMMP existence is not legal security, gain-site registration, target-condition achievement or gain-plan approval.

name: Statutory biodiversity credits
fact: Defra guidance defines statutory biodiversity credits as a last-resort BNG mechanism after on-site and off-site options and distinguishes them from private off-site biodiversity units.
gate: A credit price or theoretical credit route is not proof that the LPA accepted statutory credits for the development or that credits were purchased.

name: Statutory biodiversity credit prices
fact: Updated 2 June 2026, Defra publishes habitat-specific statutory credit prices and states prices are reviewed every 6 months.
gate: The price table is not a project cost until the exact metric shortfall, habitat type, spatial rules and credit requirement are resolved.

name: Buy statutory biodiversity credits
fact: Natural England's credit purchase service applies where developers cannot use on-site or off-site units and provides the formal purchase route.
gate: Starting a purchase or having an invoice is not proof of purchase; proof of purchase must support the Biodiversity Gain Plan where credits are used.

name: Buying statutory biodiversity credits
fact: Updated 2 June 2026, guidance describes statutory credit buying as a last resort and requires supporting metric information through the service.
gate: Credit purchase must not be treated as planning permission, gain-plan approval or evidence that on-site/off-site options were unnecessary.

name: BNG statutory credits report 2025 to 2026
fact: The 15 June 2026 annual report records £426,100 of statutory-credit income for 2025/26 and describes statutory credits as the intended last-resort backstop.
gate: National credit sales and expenditure are market/policy evidence and cannot be converted into availability or cost for a particular development.

name: What you can count towards a development's biodiversity net gain
fact: Updated 2 June 2026, guidance sets when habitat work required by other schemes can count in full, partly or not at all towards BNG.
gate: Habitat creation required for another purpose must not automatically be counted as additional BNG without applying the specific counting rules.
